sentences.text: Oligocolius is an extinct genus of mousebird from the Oligocene epoch of Germany.
Unlike modern mousebirds, the skull and beak of this animal closely resemble those of parrots.
The upper beak was deep, rounded, and possibly hooked at the tip, differing from the short beaks seen today.
A particularly long retroarticular process on the mandible provided attachment points for jaw-opening muscles.
The upper beak moved freely due to a hinge between the nasal bones and frontals, a trait similar to parrots and toucans.
The leg bone known as the tarsometatarsus was much shorter than the arm bones, unlike any other known mousebird relative.
Fossil evidence shows the species contained many fruit stones inside its body, mostly clustered beneath the skull.
This animal consumed larger fruits than living mousebirds and swallowed them whole.
The genus was described by the authority Mayr in the year 2000.
The first specimen was found in a clay pit at Frauenweiler near Wiesloch, Germany, dating to approximately 32 million years ago.
A second specimen was described by Mayr in 2013 from the 24.7 million-year-old Enspel lagerstätte.
The presence of a crop implies Oligocolius fed on tougher fruits and vegetation than living mousebirds.
Researchers infer that the crop evolved independently in Oligocolius since it is absent in living mousebirds and their close relatives.
Oligocolius likely spent more time in trees and dispersed more easily than other coliids.
Oligocolius is the only known coliid from the Oligocene epoch.
The time range for Oligocolius is from the Rupelian to the Chattian stages, between 33.9 and 23.04 million years ago.
It is uncertain if Oligocolius's adaptations were a response to a cooling climate in Europe between the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum and the Miocene Climatic Optimum.
